faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Everything you need to know about SoloDesk capabilities, data ownership, and availability.

availability.a: Account registration and authentication via Google and GitHub are live. Core business modules (Clients, Projects, Time Tracking, and Invoices) are actively in development, with foundational UI previews available to explore.

dataOwnership.q: Who owns my data and client records?
dataOwnership.a: You own 100% of your data. SoloDesk never claims ownership of your client lists, project details, logged hours, or financial records, and provides export capabilities for complete portability.

privacy.q: Does SoloDesk use third-party analytics or advertising trackers?
privacy.a: No. SoloDesk operates strictly without third-party advertising trackers or invasive behavioral tracking. Any product analytics are strictly opt-in and privacy-preserving.

languages.q: How does bilingual Arabic and English support work?
languages.a: SoloDesk is architected natively for both English and Arabic with complete right-to-left (RTL) layout switching, dedicated typography (Geist and Sahabah), and bidirectional number isolation.

devices.q: Which devices and screen sizes are supported?
devices.a: The application is fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports, tested down to 320 CSS pixels reflow and 200% browser zoom with zero horizontal scrolling.

teams.q: Can I use SoloDesk with a team or agency?
teams.a: SoloDesk is designed for freelancers and small teams. Multi-user workspace isolation and granular permission grants are currently planned on our architectural roadmap.

pricing.q: What is the pricing model for SoloDesk?
pricing.a: Pricing tiers and subscription details have not yet been announced. Early account access during our development phase is provided to explore our platform foundation.

auth.a: Authentication is powered by modern cryptographic session management via Better Auth, supporting verified OAuth providers (Google and GitHub) without storing plaintext passwords.
